title: Prostate Cancer Screening: PSA Discussion and Risk Assessment

evidenceAudit.scope: Man without symptoms of prostate cancer, seen in a Saudi primary health centre or clinic, who asks about or is eligible for prostate cancer screening: shared decision-making, who to offer a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) test and at what age, risk factors that bring screening forward, the repeat test after a high result, use of rectal examination, risk calculators and the decision to refer or to wait. Uses the 2023 American Urological Association and Society of Urologic Oncology guideline and Saudi studies. Not for men with urinary symptoms, haematuria or a known cancer, and not for treatment of prostate cancer.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national guideline on prostate cancer screening or PSA testing was found; a Saudi Ministry of Health position was not located in the sources read. The American guideline is a United States guideline and was written for United States men; its age bands and risk groups are applied to Saudi practice without local validation.

The guideline names Black ancestry, germline mutations and strong family history as risk factors; Saudi-specific risk groups, the local frequency of germline variants and local incidence were not checked and no figures are stated.

Saudi PSA reference data used: a study of 7,814 Saudi men aged 30 and over, where 90.5% had PSA between 0 and 2.5 ng/mL, and the 95th percentile rose from 3.8 ng/mL at ages 60 to 70 to 6.9 ng/mL over 71; the authors suggest age-specific thresholds. Only the abstract was available, so age bands below 60 are not stated, and the American guideline's thresholds are not Saudi-validated.
Saudi uptake data: in 6,177 men attending 48 Riyadh primary health centres in 2023 only 1.5% reported previous screening; this is self-report and limited to one city.

The guideline's benefit data come from the European and Swedish trials (reduction in metastasis and prostate cancer death at 16 to 22 years) and their balance with overdiagnosis; no Saudi trial exists and the numbers are not stated here.

Details of newer tools (secondary biomarkers, prostate magnetic resonance imaging, risk calculators) were taken only from the screening guideline summary; the biopsy-side guideline (Part II) and treatment were not read.

No medicine is part of screening, so no regimen is written; effects of drugs on PSA (for example 5-alpha reductase inhibitors) were not in the sections read and must be checked in a reference before interpreting PSA in men taking them.
A shared decision aid in Arabic was not found; the guideline cites decision aids in general only.
Figures were read by automated extraction of web text; spot-check each figure against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: PSA is a blood test made by the prostate; it is the first-line screening test, and randomised trials of PSA screening showed fewer metastases and prostate cancer deaths (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 2). PSA is not specific to cancer; a newly high result returns to normal on repeat testing in 25% to 40% of men (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 3). Screening is a preference-sensitive decision because it can find cancers that would never have caused harm (overdiagnosis) as well as aggressive ones (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 1). Black ancestry (two-fold higher risk of death), germline mutations such as BRCA2, and strong family history raise risk and justify earlier screening (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 5). Mean PSA in Saudi men aged 30 and over was 1.24 ng/mL, lower than reported in other communities (Saudi PSA reference range study, Section Results).

symptoms: Usually no symptoms: screening is for men without prostate cancer symptoms (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 1).
Men with urinary symptoms, blood in urine or bone pain need diagnostic assessment, not screening (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Section Guideline Statements).
Family history of prostate, breast or other cancers raises the question of earlier screening (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 5).
physicalSigns: Rectal examination is not recommended as the only screening test (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 8).
A suspicious rectal examination is of most use when PSA is 2 ng/mL or higher (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 8).
redFlags: Haematuria, bone pain, weight loss or acute urinary retention in a man: assess for cancer and refer; this is not screening (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Section Guideline Statements).

PSA still raised on repeat testing, or a suspicious rectal examination with raised PSA: discuss biopsy risk with the man and refer to urology (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 3, Recommendation 8 and Recommendation 10).
Known BRCA2 or other germline mutation, or a strong family history: refer for genetic counselling and start screening at 40 to 45 (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 5).
Man with a life expectancy under 10 years: screening is unlikely to benefit; discuss stopping (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 7).
precipitants: Black ancestry (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 5).
Germline mutations including BRCA1 and BRCA2 (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 5).

Strong family history: a father or brother, or two or more male relatives, with prostate cancer diagnosed before age 60, metastatic disease or death from it (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 5).
Family history of breast cancer together with prostate cancer (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 5).
Higher PSA at a young age, for example 1.3 ng/mL or more at age 40 predicted later metastasis in a Swedish cohort (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 4).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Raises PSA without cancer; urinary symptoms; PSA may fall on repeat (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 3).
Pain, fever or urinary symptoms; PSA may return to normal on repeat testing (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 3).
25% to 40% of newly high values are normal on retesting (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 3).
Persistently raised PSA, suspicious rectal examination, high calculated risk or imaging findings (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 10).
Cancer that would not have caused harm in the man's lifetime; the main harm of screening (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 7).

clinicalManagement.title: Identify men for whom screening is appropriate
actions: Consider screening for men aged 45 to 69 at average risk, from 40 to 45 if risk is increased, and for older men who are healthy with a life expectancy of at least 10 years (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 4, Recommendation 5 and Recommendation 7).
Ask about father, brothers or other male relatives with prostate cancer, breast cancer in the family, and known genetic mutations (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 5).
Do not test men who have symptoms that need a diagnostic work-up; assess them instead (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Section Guideline Statements).
Raise screening as an option, because only 1.5% of Riyadh primary care men reported having had it (Riyadh prostate cancer screening study, Section Results).

clinicalManagement.title: Hold a shared decision-making discussion
actions: Explain that PSA screening reduces metastasis and prostate cancer death in trials but can lead to overdiagnosis, extra tests and treatment side effects (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 1 and Recommendation 6).
Do not order a PSA test without telling the man, and do not fail to mention the option (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 1).
Use a decision aid if available and record his values and decision (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 1).

clinicalManagement.title: Do the PSA test
actions: Use a PSA blood test as the first test (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 2).
Compare the result with age-specific Saudi values where available (Saudi PSA reference range study, Section Conclusions).
Do not use rectal examination as the only test; add it to PSA when PSA is 2 ng/mL or higher (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 8).

clinicalManagement.title: Handle a raised PSA
actions: Repeat the PSA before any secondary biomarker, imaging or biopsy, because 25% to 40% normalise (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 3).

If still raised, consider a rectal examination, percent free PSA, prostate magnetic resonance imaging and a validated risk calculator (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 8, Recommendation 9 and Recommendation 10).
Do not use PSA velocity as the only reason for more testing (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 9).

Refer to urology for a biopsy discussion when risk is high; when risk is low the man and clinician may defer biopsy (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 10 and Recommendation 11).

clinicalManagement.title: Set the re-screening interval
actions: Every 2 to 4 years for ages 50 to 69; every 1 to 4 years for PSA 1 to 3 ng/mL; longer for PSA below 1 ng/mL (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 6 and Recommendation 7).
Shorter intervals and earlier starts for increased-risk men (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 5).
Stop or lengthen the interval after 75 if PSA is below 3 ng/mL, or when life expectancy is under 10 years (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 7).

clinicalManagement.title: Record and recall
actions: Record the discussion, PSA, rectal examination if done, plan and the date of the next review (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 7).

medicationPlan.note: No medicine is recommended in this topic. Screening uses a blood test and a conversation, and no drug treatment is part of the pathway. The effect of drugs on PSA was not in the sources read, so check a drug reference before interpreting PSA in a man on a prostate medicine.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: May offer a baseline PSA between 45 and 50 years (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 4).
Offer screening from 40 to 45 years for Black ancestry, germline mutations or strong family history (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 5).
Offer regular screening every 2 to 4 years (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 6).
1 to 4 years if PSA is 1 to 3 ng/mL; longer if below 1 ng/mL or below the age-specific median (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 7).

Age 75 or older with PSA below 3 ng/mL may stop or lengthen the interval; for men with life expectancy under 10 years screening is unlikely to help (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 7).
Repeat the PSA before any biomarker, imaging or biopsy; use of 3 ng/mL (European trial) or 4 ng/mL as thresholds is debated (AUA/SUO prostate cancer screening guideline 2023, Recommendation 3).

teaching.scope: Man without symptoms of prostate cancer, seen in a Saudi primary health centre or clinic, who asks about or is eligible for prostate cancer screening: shared decision-making, who to offer a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) test and at what age, risk factors that bring screening forward, the repeat test after a high result, use of rectal examination, risk calculators and the decision to refer or to wait. Uses the 2023 American Urological Association and Society of Urologic Oncology guideline and Saudi studies. Not for men with urinary symptoms, haematuria or a known cancer, and not for treatment of prostate cancer.
learningObjectives: Hold a shared decision conversation before any PSA test.
Offer a baseline PSA at 45 to 50, from 40 to 45 if risk is increased, and every 2 to 4 years at 50 to 69.
Repeat a raised PSA before further tests; 25% to 40% return to normal.
Stop or lengthen screening when life expectancy is under 10 years or after 75 with a low PSA.
pitfalls: Ordering PSA without telling the man.
Continuing to screen men with short life expectancy.
keyPoints: PSA velocity alone is not a reason to refer.
Rectal examination alone is not a screening test.
Symptoms need diagnostic work-up, not screening.
Saudi men have lower PSA values than other communities, but age-specific cut-offs are not yet established for practice.

patientEducation: A PSA blood test can find prostate cancer early, but it can also find slow cancers that would never have caused harm.
You and your doctor decide together whether to be tested.
A high PSA does not always mean cancer; many results return to normal when repeated.
Tell your doctor if your father, brother or other relatives had prostate cancer, or if there is breast cancer in the family.
See your doctor straight away if you have blood in the urine, pain in the bones or cannot pass urine.
lifestyleAndDiet: Keep a healthy weight and stay active.
Keep a record of your PSA results.
Discuss your family history with relatives.
mdtReferrals: Primary care physician; nurse for PSA counselling; urologist for raised PSA; radiologist for prostate magnetic resonance imaging; clinical geneticist for strong family history or mutation; pathologist.
dischargeCriteria: Shared decision recorded; PSA and any rectal examination result explained; next test date or referral arranged; symptoms that need earlier review given in writing.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Repeat PSA every 2 to 4 years at ages 50 to 69 (every 1 to 4 years if PSA is 1 to 3 ng/mL); earlier for raised PSA; review the decision to continue each time.
